Hi Asha — thanks for the clear list. I’ve pulled together a short proposal with three named tracks and a sample 6-month ramp. See the attached PDF for a printable version. High level summary below.

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-options-v2.pdf (application/pdf)

Summary (single-page):
- Track A: Onramp (conservative) — Minimum guarantee: 8 GPUs (H100 eq), warm standby: 4 GPUs; use-case: small production pilots and low concurrency microservices. Typical ramp: 8 -> 16 over 3 months.
- Track B: Production (recommended) — Minimum guarantee: 32 GPUs (mix H100/A100 depending on availability), warm standby: 8 GPUs; supports 30k qps-month conversational workloads with P95 target ~220ms using intelligent batching + KV caching. Ramp: 20% month-over-month for first 4 months, reach steady state month 5.
- Track C: Enterprise (aggressive) — Minimum guarantee: 96 GPUs, warm standby: 24 GPUs; designed for multi-region, high-throughput products with reserved burst credits for 2x peak. Ramp: staged phasing across regions - month 1 validation pool, months 2–6 phased add.

Operational controls & degradations:
- SLA-backed fallbacks: when the active pool is saturated, traffic will be routed to pre-warmed compatible model variants (lite/quantized) with graceful latency degradation.
- Burst model: monthly burst credits tied to reserved capacity allow short-term 2–3x peaks without immediate cluster resizing.
- Autoscale policy: configurable min/max per-track with cooldown windows and autoscaling hooks to Dedicated.

Rough economics (examples in attached PDF):
- Track B sample commit: 32-GPU reserved pool, 12-month term, baseline discount 18% vs pay-as-you-go; includes 10% monthly burst credits and 30-day rollout buffer.

Next steps I propose: a 30-minute alignment call with Marcus to validate expected model mix (128B vs 70B families) and Laura to review commercial terms. Can you confirm availability this week?

Thanks,
Evelyn

Thanks — quick technical clarifications and recommended adjustments:

1) Model mix & GPU equivalency: if CloudNova will use 70B models with quantization we can get similar throughput on an A100-80GB fleet vs raw H100. For latency-sensitive streams (P95 <200ms) H100 or NVLink-attached clusters are recommended.

2) Validation pool: start with a small validation cluster (4x H100 or 8x A100) in month 0 for integration tests, KV cache warmup, and prompt-engineering iterations. This reduces risk and shortens the time to 1st production traffic.

3) Batching and KV cache: our runtime benefits heavily from continuous batching; for conversational flows we recommend request sharding to preserve tail latency. Also recommend enabling prefix caching for common user flows — reduces sustained GPU pressure by ~18–25% in our benchmarks.

4) Ramp suggestion (technical): instead of flat 20% month-over-month, adopt a hybrid ramp: validation month -> +40% month 1 -> +20% month 2 -> steady additions based on weekly utilization signals. This buys a safety margin for compaction and cache warmup.

Attachment: cloudnova-sla-draft.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)
